hints.TestAddFavorite: m[person] = append(m[person], thing). Appending to a nil slice works, so a missing person is fine.
hints.TestRemove: _, ok := m[key]; delete(m, key); return ok
hints.TestWordFrequency: counts := make(map[string]int); for _, w := range words { counts[strings.ToLower(w)]++ }
hints.TestSortedKeys: Collect keys into a slice, then sort.Strings(keys) (or slices.Sort).
hints.TestTopWords: Get the keys, then sort.Slice(keys, func(i, j int) bool { if freq[keys[i]] != freq[keys[j]] { return freq[keys[i]] > freq[keys[j]] }; return keys[i] < keys[j] }), then return keys[:n] (careful if n > len).

quiz.why: A missing key yields the zero value of the element type.

quiz.q: var m map[string]int; m["a"] = 1 results in:
options: a panic: assignment to entry in nil map
quiz.why: A nil map can be read but not written. Use make or a literal.
Go deliberately randomizes map iteration order.

quiz.q: Which type can NOT be a map key?
quiz.why: Keys must be comparable. Slices are not comparable.

quiz.q: What does delete(m, "nope") do when "nope" is not in m?
quiz.why: Deleting a missing key is a no-op.
